name: Access Request Pre-Check - Risk analysis and in-flight SOD
description: Access Request Submitted event-trigger wrapper. Scores the request with custom:evaluate-access-request-risk, checks in-flight separation of duties with custom:preventive-sod-check, and answers the trigger once. Decision Variables start approved with a placeholder comment. One step per risk tier, plus one step for a detected violation, override that decision and rewrite the comment from the findings. Those four steps are the whole policy. Import disabled, set Configuration, then subscribe the event trigger to this workflow external URL as Async.

Define Variable.description: The decision and its comment, plus the findings each read copies out. Later steps read these variables, not the Get Accounts steps, so a retry read can refill them without rewiring anything downstream. The step key must stay Define Variable: ISC builds the defineVariable paths from it and rejects update steps that target any other key.

Get Access Token.description: Set basic auth on this step to the workflow OAuth client. Do not store the secret in this export.

Check Invoke Result.description: The connector returns HTTP 200 even when the operation failed. Catch that here so a leftover result account cannot look like a scored request.

Check Risk Result.description: The result account can exist before its attributes are indexed, so an absent tier here is a read that was too early, not a failure yet.

Wait For Risk Result.description: One pause before the single retry read. Wait steps are minute-granular, and this only costs time on requests whose result was not readable yet.

Read Risk Result Retry.description: Same filter as Read Risk Result. Keep the two in step.

Check Risk Result Retry.description: The retry is the last word. Still no tier means the risk evaluation did not produce one.

Set Risk Values.description: Copies the first read into the variables the tier steps compare.

Set Risk Values Retry.description: Same copy from the retry read, into the same variables.

Call Preventive Sod Check.description: Request mode. Passing the access request id reports only the violations this request would introduce. Inflight Only (default true) skips existing active violations.

Check Sod Invoke Result.description: The connector returns HTTP 200 even when the operation failed. Catch that here so a leftover result account cannot look like a scored request.

Read Sod Result.description: The filter must match the requestId sent to the operation, which is the identity it persists under.

Check Sod Result.description: A SoD check that produced no answer never counts as a passing one. The summary is the presence sentinel because it is always written, while the violation flag is legitimately false on a clean result.

Wait For Sod Result.description: One pause before the single retry read, as on the risk side.

Read Sod Result Retry.description: Same filter as Read SoD Result. Keep the two in step.

Check Sod Result Retry.description: The retry is the last word. Still no summary means the SoD check did not produce an answer.

Set Sod Values.description: Copies the summary only. The violation flag is set by the next step so the account read, where the flag is a real boolean, is what BooleanEquals compares.

Set Sod Values Retry.description: Same copy from the retry read, into the same variable.

Check Sod Violation Flag.description: Reads the flag straight off the account, where it is a real boolean, and turns it into a literal on the variable.

Check Sod Violation Flag Retry.description: Same read on the retry account. Both branches land on the same two setter steps.

Set Evaluation Failed.description: Every failed token, invoke, or result read lands here, as does an unknown risk tier and a missing SoD result.

End Success.description: The Access Request Submitted callback was sent.

Callback Approved.description: Sends the approval to the trigger. The decision is a hardcoded boolean: a path substitution renders it as the string "true" or "false", which the trigger rejects.

Callback Denied.description: Sends the denial to the trigger. The decision is a hardcoded boolean: a path substitution renders it as the string "true" or "false", which the trigger rejects.

Check Approved.description: Picks the callback that carries the matching literal. Splitting the send is the only way to put a real boolean in the body, since the decision cannot be templated in as one. Update Variable stores the decision as the string "true" or "false", so it is compared as a string here. BooleanEquals never matches a variable that Update Variable wrote, and every path into this step writes the decision first.
